name: Oma Skat
summary: Two-player variant of Skat where a face-down dummy third hand contributes a random card to each trick.
rules_text: Play with a standard 32-card Skat deck. Deal as in three-hand Skat: two players get hands, and a third pile is the Oma facing down. The Oma never bids; the two live players bid against each other to become declarer. Declarer chooses the game type. Play tricks sequentially. In each trick the two players play one card following suit if possible, and the top card of the Oma pile is turned face up as the third card. Oma does not have to follow suit or trump. The trick is won by the highest legal card among the three by normal Skat rules. In a common variation the Oma card is not contested but simply given to the winner of the two-card trick. Scoring otherwise uses normal Skat rules. Because Oma plays randomly, null games are much harder.
